item.title: [preventOrFixIssue] Power Platform – Recreate connections made to the Azure DevOps connector prior to September 2024
item.description:
We identified that an app, flow, or agent in your environment utilizes a connection to the Azure DevOps connector that was created prior to September 1, 2024. These connections use a legacy app registration method for authentication, which is being removed. Once removed, any flow, app, or agent using those connections will no longer be able to authenticate.

The removal of the legacy app registration method has been started and will be completed by November 30, 2026.

What action do I need to take?
Identify any Azure DevOps connections in your environment(s) created before September 1, 2024. Once identified take the following actions:
  • Create a new Azure DevOps connection and complete the consent prompt.
  • Update any flows, canvas apps, or agents that reference the old connection to use the new connection.
  • Delete the old connection once no resources in your environment are referencing it.
Why is this action needed?
Removal of the legacy app registration method will cause any flow, app, or agent utilizing a connection made to the Azure DevOps connector prior to September 1, 2024, to fail to authenticate. If action is not taken, your flows, apps and agents utilizing those connections will stop functioning as expected.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Automatic recording and transcription options align with admin policies
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is updating the Record and transcribe automatically setting in Meeting options, so meeting organizers see only the automatic recording and transcription options permitted by their assigned Teams meeting policies. This change reduces confusion, improves policy compliance, and helps ensure organizers cannot select options that are unavailable based on organizational settings.

As part of this update, Teams will introduce a new Record only option that automatically starts meeting recording without starting transcription.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early December 2026 and expected to complete by mid-December 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Teams administrators who manage meeting recording and transcription policies
  • Meeting organizers who configure automatic recording or transcription settings in Meeting options

Platforms and services

  • Teams desktop, web, and mobile clients that support Meeting Options.

What will happen

  • Meeting organizers will only see automatic recording and transcription options allowed by their effective Teams meeting policy.
  • Policy evaluation respects policies assigned directly to a user, inherited through group assignment, or applied through the global policy.
  • A new Record only option will be available when recording is permitted by policy.

  • The available automatic options for each policy combination are shown below:
Recording policyTranscription policyAutomatic options available in Meeting Options
AllowedAllowedRecord and transcribe; Transcribe only; Record only; Off
AllowedBlockedRecord only; Off
BlockedAllowedTranscribe only; Off
BlockedBlockedThe automatic setting is not shown

[Action required and recommendations]

No admin action is required; the feature is enabled automatically as part of the service update.

We recommend that:

  • Inform meeting organizers about the new Record only option.
  • Communicate that available automatic recording and transcription options are now determined by the organizer's assigned Teams meeting policies.
  • Review recording and transcription policies if you want to understand which options organizers in your organization will see.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Excel: Changes to Get Data from Web (Legacy) experience
item.description:
[What and Why:]

To import data from the web with Power Query, use the newer Get Data from Web experience. The existing Get Data from Web (Legacy) functionality will be reduced. The newer experience provides modern authentication, table detection, data transformation, and refresh capabilities.

Existing queries that use the legacy experience will continue to refresh.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): We will begin rolling out in mid-January 2027 and expect to complete by early April 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

After this change:

  • Users will no longer be able to create new legacy web queries with the dialog accessed through Get Data > Legacy Wizards > From Web (Legacy) or edit existing ones.
  • Existing legacy web queries in workbooks will continue to refresh, and users can continue to edit refresh properties through Queries & Connections > Properties > Refresh control UI.
  • Programmatic attempts to open the legacy New Web Query dialog will return an error.
  • Programmatic attempts to create legacy Web Query connections will continue to work.
  • Creating legacy Web Query connections through an .iqy file will continue to work.
  • Other legacy data import wizards are not affected by this change.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

You may want to update internal training and documentation because users will receive this change automatically as it progresses through deployment rings.

Consider migrating web queries to the newer Get Data from Web experience:

  1. Right-click the section of imported data that you want to migrate.
  2. Select Edit query.
  3. Copy the URL from the address bar.
  4. From the Data tab, select From Web in the Get & Transform Data section.
  5. Paste the URL into the address bar and follow the steps to create the new web query.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot offer and name updates
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We're updating Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription names to make purchasing requirements clearer.

Beginning October 16, 2026, existing Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names. Examples include Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on) and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (add-on).

The "(add-on)" designation reflects the qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement for these existing subscriptions. Beginning December 1, 2026, new Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions can be purchased without a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • October 16, 2026: Microsoft 365 Copilot subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will include "(add-on)" in their names.
  • December 1, 2026: New Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions can be purchased without a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription and will not include "(add-on)" in their names.
  • December 1, 2026: Existing add-on subscriptions will reach end of sale for new purchases. This is not end of life: You can continue to renew your subscriptions and add or reduce seats as you do today.
  • Existing subscriptions will retain "(add-on)" in their names.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Organizations with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft 365 Copilot Business subscriptions.

What will happen:

  • Existing subscriptions that require a qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription will be renamed: 
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot (add-on)
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot Business (add-on)
  • Your subscription, service, pricing, licensing rights, and renewal eligibility remain unchanged.
  • No migration or license reassignment is required.
  • The name update does not change Copilot capabilities, which continue to depend on the apps and services you're licensed for.
  • Self-service purchase (SSP) and end-user trials within Microsoft 365 products will continue to be available with this update.
  • Beginning December 1, 2026, new subscriptions without the qualifying Microsoft 365 base subscription requirement will be available without "(add-on)" in their names.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No action is required for most organizations.

  • Do not migrate subscriptions or reassign licenses solely because of the name update.
  • If you use PowerShell scripts or license management processes that reference product names, update them to use product or SKU IDs before October 16, 2026.
  • Consider updating internal documentation that references the current subscription names.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Entra: Windows Hello for Business and macOS Platform SSO as standalone MFA factors
item.description:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

Microsoft Entra will soon recognize Windows Hello for Business (WHfB) and macOS Platform Single Sign-On (PSSO) as standalone multifactor authentication (MFA) factors in supported authentication scenarios.

Today, WHfB and macOS PSSO can satisfy MFA requirements during primary sign-in, but users may still be required to register and use an additional passkey or authentication method for certain step-up authentication prompts, Authentication Strength policies, and sign-in frequency checks.

After this rollout, users who authenticate with WHfB or macOS PSSO will be able to satisfy supported MFA requirements without registering an additional passkey. This change helps organizations expand the use of phishing-resistant authentication methods and reduce reliance on less secure authentication methods. As part of this change, a user's WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials will be displayed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete in mid-December 2026 (previously late November)

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra ID
  • Users who authenticate with Windows Hello for Business
  • Users who authenticate with macOS Platform SSO
  • Organizations using Conditional Access Authentication Strength policies

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Windows Hello for Business
  • macOS Platform SSO
  • Conditional Access
  • Authentication Strength policies

What will happen

After rollout:

  • Users signing in with WHfB or macOS PSSO can complete supported MFA challenges without requiring a separate passkey.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO will satisfy supported MFA requirements for step-up authentication scenarios.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported Authentication Strength policy requirements.
  • WHfB and macOS PSSO can be used during 2FA to satisfy supported sign-in frequency challenge requirements.
  • Users whose only MFA method is WHfB or macOS PSSO will be considered MFA-capable.
  • Users who sign in with only a password will no longer be automatically prompted to register an additional MFA method if WHfB or macOS PSSO is their only registered MFA credential.
  • Users with WHfB or macOS PSSO credentials, will be able to see them listed in My Security Info as auto-registered passkeys.

[Action required and recommendations]

No configuration changes are required.

We recommend reviewing user onboarding and MFA registration processes before rollout. Because WHfB and macOS PSSO credentials are device-bound, users may not be able to complete MFA challenges from devices where those credentials are not available.

Recommended actions:

  • Update onboarding guidance to ensure users register at least one portable MFA method.
  • Consider requiring users to register a synced passkey or Microsoft Authenticator passkey in addition to WHfB or macOS PSSO.
  • Review custom Authentication Strength policies to confirm WHfB and macOS PSSO are allowed where appropriate.
  • Update user documentation because users with only WHfB or macOS PSSO registered will no longer be automatically guided to register an additional MFA method.

Learn more (To be updated closer to GA rollout.)

  • Plan a Windows Hello for Business deployment | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn
  • Prepare users to provision and use Windows Hello for Business | Security | Windows | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Microsoft 365 Copilot: Schedule prompts in Agent Builder
item.description:
Updated October 13, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[Introduction]

We’re introducing the ability to create workflows that schedule prompts in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot. This new capability allows users to schedule prompts that run automatically on a defined cadence, such as hourly, daily, or weekly. Based on customer feedback requesting more automation and proactive insights, workflows help users reduce manual prompting and automate routine tasks using their Copilot agents.

[When this will happen]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout is expected to begin end of October 2026 (previously early September) and complete by end of November 2026 (previously end of September).

[How this affects your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users who create and manage agents using Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 Copilot (Premium)

What will happen

  • Users will be able to create scheduled workflows for agents.
  • Scheduled workflows include:
    • Prompt text
    • Triggers and recurrence patterns
    • Date, time, and time zone settings
  • Supported recurrence patterns:
    • Hourly
    • Daily
    • Weekly
    • Monthly
    • Yearly
  • Workflows are configured per user and run only for the user who created them.
  • Workflows are not shared when an agent is shared with others.
  • Scheduled workflows will not run for draft or unpublished agents.
  • Users can view, edit, preview, and delete workflows within Agent Builder.
  • This feature is enabled by default and respects existing tenant and Copilot policies.

Screenshot of Agent Builder showing a “Project Horizon” agent configuration screen. The instructions panel is visible in the center, while a dropdown menu in the top-right corner is expanded with options including “Create a workflow for this agent” and “Manage workflows.” A purple arrow highlights the option to create a new workflow.

 

Screenshot of Agent Builder showing a “Project Horizon” agent configuration screen. A modal titled “Create a workflow to prompt your agent” is centered, with a text field labeled “Prompt” and scheduling options set to run weekly on Friday at 1:30 PM. A purple arrow highlights where to enter the prompt. 

[What you can do to prepare]

  • No admin action is required to enable this feature.
  • Consider informing users who build Copilot agents about the availability of workflows.
  • Update internal documentation or training materials if you support Copilot agent creation.
  • For privacy or compliance requests, continue using the existing Data Subject Request (DSR) processes.

Learn more: Dsr Compliance - Delete Flow | Dsr Compliance | Power Platform API | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does this change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Existing customer data may be processed automatically based on a time-based trigger rather than direct user initiation. The scope of data access remains unchanged and follows existing permissions.
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, ML, or agent capabilities that interact with customer data?Yes. This change introduces a new agent capability that allows Copilot agents to run prompts automatically on a defined schedule, instead of only responding to manual prompts.
Does this change provide a new way for users to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can now interact with generative AI asynchronously through scheduled workflows that execute prompts on their behalf.
Can users enable or disable this feature themselves?Yes. Users can create, edit, disable, or delete scheduled workflows for their agents at any time.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Planner: AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing AI-generated status reports in Planner Agent. This feature uses Planner plan data to generate a status report that summarizes overall status, progress, risks, and next steps. Users can customize reports by specifying items such as audience, tone, length, reporting period, and report sections before reviewing and refining the generated content.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): Rollout has completed.
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by mid-November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations who have Planner agent enabled as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Within those organizations, users with an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license who use Planner Agent.
    • Note: Users who view or edit reports do not require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license; a Copilot license is required only to generate reports.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Planner
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Planner Agent will be able to generate AI-powered status reports from Planner plan data within Microsoft 365 Copilot app.
  • Reports will be generated only from Planner content that users already have permission to access. Existing Planner sharing permissions, Copilot policies, and agent controls continue to apply.
  • Reports will synthesize plan information, including tasks, owners, due dates, status, buckets, and recent activity, into sections such as executive summary, progress, risks and blockers, achievements, milestones, and next steps.
  • Users can customize reports by reporting period, sections, tone, length, audience, and additional instructions before reviewing and refining the generated content.
  • Reports can be exported to a Copilot Page and shared by link or exported to Word and PDF.
  • This feature adds new functionality and does not replace existing Planner capabilities.

Copilot-generated status report

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required. We recommend that you:

  • Confirm that intended users have an active Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Review Planner Agent and Copilot agent availability and settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center. If needed, the agent can be blocked tenant-wide.
  • Inform support teams and users about the new status report generating capability, which can be accessed via the Planner Agent in Copilot or the Reports tab in Planner.
    • Note that generating a report requires a plan that is shared with a Microsoft 365 Group and contains sufficient task data.
  • Update internal documentation, training, and change management materials as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations]

To assist our customers with identifying compliance concerns, review the questions below and provide details for impact if appropriate:

  • Does the change store new customer data?
    • [Answer] Yes. A status report generated from your plan appears in the Microsoft 365 Copilot conversation. If a user chooses to export it, the report is also saved as a copilot page or a word document.
  • Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)?
    • [Answer] Yes. When an authorized user requests a report, Planner Agent uses information from a plan they can access to create a status report. If the user attaches a file as a template, that file will also be used for the request. This change does not edit the source plan or its tasks.
  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?
    • [Answer] Yes. It adds the ability to generate and refine a status report through Planner Agent chat using accessible plan information. It does not grant the agent access to plans the requesting user cannot access.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Teams: Video sharing from OneDrive in Teams events
item.description:

Organizers and producers using Manage what attendees see can load videos from OneDrive and present them on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos in PowerPoint. This improvement provides smoother, higher-quality video playback for attendees and simplifies event production through built-in video playback controls.

Platforms and services

  • OneDrive
  • Teams events

  • Videos can be presented on stage without screen sharing a local media player or embedding videos into a PowerPoint presentation.

item.title: [planForChange] Action may be required: Review who can create agents in Microsoft Entra
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Entra is changing who can create agent blueprints by default. Starting November 4, default users will be able to create new agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off Users can create agent blueprints. This means that users without built-in or custom Entra roles will be able to create new agent blueprints in their organization. From now until rollout begins, you can set your tenant preferences to prepare for this rollout. If you do not want users in your organization to create new agent blueprints and their identities, follow the instructions below. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • Worldwide: Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra
  • Default users who don't have a built-in or custom Microsoft Entra role

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

  • Default users will be able to create agent blueprints unless an administrator turns off Users can create agent blueprints. If you set the toggle to No, default users will not be able to create new agents. Supported administrators and users assigned the Agent ID Developer role can continue to create them. 
  • If you change this toggle now, your tenant won't change right away. Your setting takes effect when the rollout begins in early November.

[Action required and recommendations]

If default users should be allowed to create agents in your organization, no action is required. Choosing to allow users to create agent blueprints will not begin until the functionality is available in your tenant.

To restrict creation:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center using this link.
  2. Go to Entra ID > Users > User settings.
  3. Under Default user role permissions, find Users can create agent blueprints.
  4. Set the toggle to No, then save the change.

For more information and instructions on setting the toggle for your organization, see Manage who can create agent blueprints here.

This change affects new agent blueprint creation by default users. It does not:

  • Change or remove existing agent blueprints.
  • Change who can create agent identities from existing blueprints.
  • Block an app or an agent from creating identities
  • Affect creation requirements within platforms such as Microsoft Foundry or Security Copilot, such as requiring licenses and Azure subscriptions.

The new setting is independent of Users can register applications. Review both settings separately.

Learn more

  • Delegate application management administrator permissions - Microsoft Entra ID | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Entra: Changes to AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager permission for agent identities
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Entra Agent ID is enforcing tighter restrictions for autonomous creation of an agent’s own identities. Currently, all agents are granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager upon creation without administrator approval. Starting November 4, Microsoft Entra will no longer automatically grant AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agent blueprint principals, and creation of identities will need an admin to grant consent.

Agents that use app-only authentication to create their own agent identities must be explicitly granted the AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission or move to another supported authorization model before enforcement reaches their tenant.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Entra 
  • No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Entra

What will happen

Today, an agent blueprint principal is granted AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager automatically. This implicit grant allows the principal to create agent identities without a tenant-admin granting an app-role assignment.

After enforcement, an administrator must grant the Microsoft Graph application permission AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager to agents that needs this authority.

This change:

  • Makes app-only agent identity creation authority visible, auditable, and revocable.
  • Makes AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager revocable if consented
  • Affects existing and future agents.
  • Doesn't remove existing agent identities or agent blueprints.
  • Doesn't remove the ability for agent identity blueprints to create agent identities, when AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager is explicitly granted by an administrator
  • Doesn't affect an agent that uses a directory role to authorize creation of agent identities.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if your organization doesn't have an agent that depends on the automatic AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager grant.

Identify agents that create agent identities without a signed-in user.

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Audit Logs.
  3. Set the Category to "ApplicationManagement"
  4. Set the Activity filter to "Add Service Principal"

Find events where the Initiated By (actor) Type is Application and the Target is an agent identity.

For each affected agent:

  1. Sign in to the Microsoft Entra admin center.
  2. Go to Entra ID>Agent blueprints>Search for your agent blueprint>Granted permissions
  3. Review if the Agent has any other granted permissions that may allow for creation of agent identities. If there are no other permissions allowing for creation, this agent relies on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager.
  4. Starting October 16, you may grant the explicit AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager Microsoft Graph application permission through tenant-wide admin consent or manual app-role creation. Granting it earlier will cause an error. A successful grant appears in the Granted Permissions table with “An administrator” in the Granted By column.
  5. Test app-only agent identity creation before enforcement begins.
  6. Update operational guidance for a failed request after enforcement.

If an app-only request relies only on the automatic grant after enforcement reaches your tenant, the request will fail with a 403 authorization error.

Learn more

  • For more about how to grant your agents access to resources, visit Grant agents access to Microsoft 365 resources | Microsoft Learn. 
  • For the Microsoft Graph permission reference on AgentIdentity.CreateAsManager, visit Microsoft Graph permissions reference - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn.

[Compliance considerations]

No specific compliance impacts have been identified for this configuration update.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Agent 365: Expanded access to Microsoft agent usage and activity insights in Microsoft 365 admin center
item.description:
[What and why]

We’re removing the Agent 365 license requirement for observability data for supported agents built by Microsoft or on Microsoft platforms. This change expands access to usage and activity insights in the Microsoft 365 admin center, helping administrators monitor how agents are used.

This change is limited to observability metrics. It does not remove licensing requirements for other Agent 365 capabilities or for agent activity metrics for agents built on third-party platforms.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in late November 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using supported agents built by Microsoft or on Microsoft platforms

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Agent 365 observability

What will happen

  • An Agent 365 license will no longer be required to view usage and activity metrics for supported agents built by Microsoft or on Microsoft platforms.
  • The change applies to both existing and new supported agents.
  • In Registry, the affected usage and activity columns are Active users, Total sessions, Exception rate, and Run Time.
  • In Agent overview, affected cards and charts include Active users, Active users over time, and Trending agents by active users. These views may already be visible in organizations without an Agent 365 license. Reported values and trends may change temporarily as activity data accumulates during rollout.
  • In Agent details > Activity, affected metrics include the Active users, Sessions, Exceptions, and Agent run-time cards, and the Active users over time and Sessions over time charts.
  • As the change reaches your organization, some metrics may initially appear lower or show incomplete trends while activity data is collected. This temporary change does not necessarily indicate reduced agent usage.
  • Allow up to 30 days after data collection begins for a full 30-day reporting view for each enabled agent or platform. Completing the rollout does not mean every agent will immediately have a full 30-day history.
  • Data availability continues to depend on the agent or platform sending activity data and on applicable observability settings.
  • Existing licensing and access requirements for third-party agent observability are unchanged.
  • Other licensed Agent 365 capabilities, including risk-related features, continue to require the applicable license.

[Action required and recommendations]

When comparing usage before and after rollout, account for the time required to collect a full reporting window rather than interpreting a lower displayed value alone as a decline in usage.

Review the affected Microsoft 365 admin center views as the change reaches your organization.

Learn more

  • Data handling, data residency, and compliance in Agent 365 observability | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations were identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot Business: New service plan for subscription identification
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft is introducing a new service plan unique to Microsoft 365 Copilot Business and Microsoft 365 Business with Copilot subscriptions. The service plan provides a consistent way to identify eligible business subscriptions and enables more precise service administration as offerings and workloads evolve.

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
Beginning November 9, 2026, we are introducing staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications. The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

If no corrective action is initiated after repeated notifications, when a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 90 days from the date the tenant exceeds capacity, affected sandbox environments will be disabled and will no longer be accessible to users. During this phase customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed.

Production environments are not subject to administration mode and disabled stage restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox or production type environments will remain blocked while the tenant is over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 14, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The following products are included in the storage validation rollout:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations for sandbox and production type environments are blocked immediately when the tenant exceeds its entitled capacity.
2. Administration mode After 30 unresolved days from T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 90 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from accessing *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation. During this phase, customers can contact Microsoft Support for the sole purpose of directing data export options, if needed. All other mechanisms designed to resolve overage are also available to customers at this phase.

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant’s current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, future restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Restrictions are removed after the tenant has returned below 100% of its entitled storage capacity. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before November 9, 2026:
  • Review Database, File, and Log capacity in the Power Platform admin center.
  • Remove or archive data that is no longer needed.
  • Establish data governance policies in your environment to help prevent future storage overages.
  • Purchase additional capacity or configure pay-as-you-go.
  • Inform administrators, makers, and users about the potential restrictions.
  • Review your release activities that depend on sandbox availability, and plan accordingly.
For additional information, please visit the following articles:
  • What happens when my organization exceeds storage capacity?
  • Dataverse capacity-based storage details
  • Manage data with Dataverse governance policies
  • Free up storage space
  • Add more Dataverse capacity
  • Configure pay-as-you-go in your environment
  • What environments consume tenant capacity
  • Power Platform licensing guidance
*Affected environments: Sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go enabled. Any references to affected environments in this message apply exclusively to those sandbox environments.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Purview Audit: AuditLogQuery API generally available and Search-UnifiedAuditLog retiring
item.description:
[What and why]

The Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API is generally available for programmatic access to Microsoft Purview Audit activity logs. We are also announcing the planned retirement of the Search-UnifiedAuditLog PowerShell cmdlet on October 15, 2027.

The AuditLogQuery API provides improved scalability and reliability, more granular workload-level permissions, and support for exporting up to 1 million audit records per query. As audit data volumes and automation scenarios have grown, Search-UnifiedAuditLog has reached scalability limitations that can affect reliability and performance for large-volume searches. Future investments and enhancements for audit search will focus on the AuditLogQuery API.

[Rollout schedule] 

Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API general availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026

Search-UnifiedAuditLog retirement:

  • Search-UnifiedAuditLog will continue to function unchanged until October 15, 2027.
  • On October 15, 2027, Search-UnifiedAuditLog will be retired and will no longer provide access to the audit log.
  • Organizations using Search-UnifiedAuditLog should migrate to the Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API before October 15, 2027.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations that use Search-UnifiedAuditLog for audit data retrieval, reporting, investigations, compliance workflows, or automation are affected.
  • Organizations that do not use Search-UnifiedAuditLog are not required to take action for this retirement.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Purview Audit
  • Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API
  • Exchange PowerShell Search-UnifiedAuditLog cmdlet

What will happen

  • Admins with the required permissions will be able to programmatically access audit logs through the Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API.
  • Existing PowerShell scripts, applications, and automation workflows that call Search-UnifiedAuditLog will need to be updated to use the AuditLogQuery API.
  • Search-UnifiedAuditLog will continue to function unchanged until October 15, 2027.
  • On October 15, 2027, Search-UnifiedAuditLog will no longer provide access to the audit log.
  • There is no tenant setting to prevent the retirement.
  • Organizations that do not complete migration before October 15, 2027, may experience disruptions to audit retrieval processes that depend on Search-UnifiedAuditLog.
  • Future investments and enhancements for audit search will focus on the AuditLogQuery API rather than Search-UnifiedAuditLog.
  • The AuditLogQuery API supports exporting up to 1 million audit records per query.
  • The AuditLogQuery API uses tenant-level throttling limits. Each tenant has a baseline of 200 search submissions per rolling 24-hour period and can have up to 50 searches queued or running at one time. Larger tenants may receive higher allocations based on eligible license counts.
  • When a limit is reached, the API returns an HTTP 429 Too Many Requests response with retry guidance.

[Action required and recommendations]

  • If your organization uses Search-UnifiedAuditLog, begin migration planning and complete the migration before October 15, 2027.
  • Identify scripts, applications, automation workflows, and operational processes that currently use Search-UnifiedAuditLog.
  • Evaluate the Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API and validate that it meets your audit retrieval requirements.
  • Register your application with Microsoft Graph and add the required Microsoft Graph permissions.
  • Update and test existing integrations to use the AuditLogQuery API.
  • Complete migration before October 15, 2027, to avoid service disruption.

No action is required if your organization does not use Search-UnifiedAuditLog.

Learn more

  • auditLogQuery resource type - Microsoft Graph v1.0 | Microsoft Learn
  • Examples - List auditLogQueries - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn
  • Get started with auditing solutions | Microsoft Learn
  • Learn about auditing solutions in Microsoft Purview | Microsoft Learn
  • Microsoft Graph service-specific throttling limits - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn
  • Permissions - List auditLogQueries - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn
  • Search-UnifiedAuditLog (ExchangePowerShell) | Microsoft Learn
  • Security audit log query service limits - Microsoft Graph service-specific throttling limits - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn
  • Use the Microsoft Graph API - Microsoft Graph | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable Audit logging capabilities?Search-UnifiedAuditLog will no longer provide access to the Audit log effective October 15, 2027.
Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities?Programmatic retrieval of Microsoft Purview Audit activity logs is moving from Search-UnifiedAuditLog to the Microsoft Graph AuditLogQuery API for organizations using the retiring cmdlet.
Does the change include an admin control?Access to the AuditLogQuery API requires applicable Microsoft Graph permissions. The retirement itself cannot be prevented through a tenant setting. The source does not state that the change can be controlled through Entra ID group membership.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Meeting memory file generation
item.description:
Updated October 12, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why]

Microsoft Teams is introducing AI generated meeting memory files that capture key insights from meetings (formerly archive files). These files help Microsoft 365 Copilot and Facilitator deliver more accurate context aware responses while maintaining strong privacy controls by not storing raw meeting content. This capability supports enterprise ready AI by improving knowledge grounding while keeping data secure and manageable.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 558933.

[Rollout Schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning early November 2026 (previously early October) and expected to complete mid-November 2026 (previously mid-October)
  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning early December 2026 (previously mid-October) and expected to complete early January 2027 (previously late October 2026)

Teams admin center controls for this feature will be available approximately four weeks before memory file generation begins. The dates above reflect when admin controls become available.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams administrators
  • Users with Microsoft 365 Copilot or Facilitator capabilities enabled

Platforms/Services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • SharePoint Embedded

What will happen

  • AI meeting memory files (.meeting files) will be generated for meetings where Intelligent Recap is turned on. The feature is enabled by default in your organization.
  • Memory files are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container, not in user storage. You can control the default expiration time for these files within your organization.
  • Users cannot directly view or access memory files.
  • When the feature is released, Facilitator will use the memory to answer questions about meetings and responses include citations linking to meeting recaps or invites. In the future, Copilot will also use the memory to answer questions about meetings. 
  • Memory files cannot be modified, renamed, or moved.
  • All content in memory files is AI-generated. No raw transcript snippets are stored.
  • Memory generation requires all of the following:
    • Meeting memory is enabled for your organization.
    • Intelligent Recap is enabled for the meeting.
  • Memory files are not created for:
    • Meetings with sensitivity labels that include encryption
    • End-to-end encrypted meetings
    • Meetings with restricted copying or forwarding
  • Access and data protection:
    • Only users with access to the meeting can receive responses grounded in its memory and AI tools do not surface insights to users who do not have meeting access.
    • Memory knowledge is only shared with users who are in the same tenant as the meeting organizer.

[Action Required / Recommendations]

No immediate action is required. However, administrators should review configuration settings and consider organizational policy alignment.

Admins can enable or disable this feature in the Teams admin center.

Recommended actions:

  • Review the AI archive setting in Teams admin center before rollout. Setting path: Meeting Policies > Meeting Memory".
  • Evaluate the default expiration period, which is set to five years (1,825 days), and adjust retention settings as needed to align with compliance policies.
  • Communicate this capability to helpdesk teams and compliance stakeholders.
  • Monitor availability of the memory setting in Teams admin center and review or update settings when they become available. Memory file generation will begin 4 weeks after the setting is released to your organization.

Learn more: AI Archives for Microsoft Teams Meetings | Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn 

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data, and if so, where, and is the data cached or permanently stored?Yes. The change introduces AI-generated meeting memory files that are stored in a tenant-owned SharePoint Embedded container and retained according to a configurable retention period.
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Meeting transcripts and metadata are processed into structured AI memory files that enable downstream AI systems such as Copilot and Facilitator to reason over meeting content.
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI or machine learning capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. Copilot and Facilitator use AI meeting memory files to generate context-aware responses grounded in prior meeting content.
Does the change provide users any new way of interacting with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with Copilot and Facilitator, which leverage meeting memory  data to answer questions and provide insights about meetings.
Does the change modify retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows?Yes. AI meeting memory files are governed by a default retention period of five years and are automatically deleted upon expiration.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can enable or disable AI meeting memory generation and configure retention settings in the Teams Admin Center.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Copilot: New ways to work across Microsoft Copilot and Microsoft 365
item.description:

[What and why:]

Updates include a new Home experience and enhanced Office capabilities in the Copilot app; Code and Autopilot for building solutions and automating work; an enterprise-grade platform for running code; and updates to Copilot Notebooks, Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive, and Work IQ.

Home in the Copilot app:

  • When users open the Copilot app, they will land in Home, which brings Chat and Cowork together on one screen. Users can switch between Chat and Cowork in the prompt box. Read more in the blog. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • As part of this update, we are making the following updates to the left navigation pane: 1) Plugins will replace the standalone Agents entry point (called Agents & Skills for some preview users) from Chat and the Customize entry point from Cowork. 2) For users with access to Cowork, Automations from Cowork will move to the Home navigation pane. These updates will roll out to Frontier in October for all Microsoft 365 users with access to the Copilot app.
  • Researcher and Analyst will no longer be pinned by default in the Copilot app navigation pane. Users can continue to access these agents from Plugins and can pin them to the navigation pane based on their preferences. Organizations that want these agents to remain pinned for their users can pre-pin them through the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Chat can complete long-running, multi-step knowledge work, including drafting email, managing meetings, working in Teams, managing OneDrive and SharePoint files, finding people, and creating Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, and HTML files. Sensitive actions require user approval. Users can track and manage their long-running activity from Chat in the Tasks view, accessible in the upper right of the Copilot app navigation pane. These capabilities will roll out to Frontier later this month and are available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.
  • Chat will begin surfacing Skills that are used while generating responses, giving users greater transparency into how Copilot responds. This update will begin worldwide rollout in October and is available to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

Code:

  • The new Code experience gives users a dedicated place in the Copilot app to create trackers, dashboards, and apps using natural language. Users can access Code by going to the Code tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Code uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • Code is rolling out to Frontier later this month.
  • To prepare: To enable Copilot Code for your tenant, admin must deploy the unified app and set the target channel to beta.

Autopilot:

  • Autopilot, previously called Scout, is an always-on personal agent in the Copilot app with persistent context, identity, and memory. Users can access Autopilot by going to the Autopilot tab in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Autopilot uses usage-based billing. Eligible users require a Microsoft 365 Copilot license and spending policy.
  • We will update this message with rollout timing and admin control details when available.

Copilot app UI updates:

  • Cowork, Code, and Autopilot entry points in the Copilot app will be visible by default to users with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license. Users that do not have a spending policy enabled will not be able to access these capabilities; instead, they will see an in-product message after clicking on the entry points to request access or learn more.
  • A new Microsoft 365 admin center setting will let admins choose whether users without a spending policy see Request Access or Learn More. Admins can configure whether or not users can request Copilot credits to use these experiences. Admins can also choose to block requests.
  • The existing setting in the admin center used to hide usage-based experiences (“Allow users to discover and use AI experiences enabled by usage-based billing”) will be removed.
  • By default, enterprise users without a spending policy will see the “request access” message. Education users will see a Learn More link and cannot request access.
  • This update will roll out to standard customers in October and deferred customers in November.
  • To prepare: Review Microsoft 365 Admin center settings for usage-based experiences and spending policy. Decide if you want users without a spending policy to receive a "Request access" or "Learn more" message.

Full Office capabilities in the Copilot app:

  • Users can use full Word, Excel, and PowerPoint creation, editing, and collaboration capabilities in the Copilot app, side by side with Copilot. Users can also access recent Word, Excel, and PowerPoint files from Library in the Copilot app navigation pane. Read more in the blog.
  • Capabilities accessed through Chat are included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license. Capabilities accessed through Cowork use usage-based billing.
  • These capabilities are rolling out to Frontier later this month.

Copilot Managed Runtime:

  • Copilot Managed Runtime is an enterprise-grade platform for running code within the Microsoft 365 tenant boundary under IT governance. It supports apps built in Code, Cowork, Copilot Studio, and supported command-line and SDK experiences. Admins can manage these apps in the Microsoft 365 admin center. Read more in the blog.
  • Managed Runtime is starting to roll out now into public preview.

Copilot Notebooks updates:

  • Copilot Notebooks will add task delegation, full Office editing and collaboration, interactive report creation, audio overview updates, model selection, and an updated user experience in the Copilot app and OneNote.
  • These updates will roll out to Frontier later this month.

SharePoint and OneDrive updates:

  • We are announcing the general availability of Copilot in SharePoint. The everyday AI capabilities that have been in public preview stay included with a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). New agentic capabilities and the ability to work at greater scale than was possible in preview will be available through usage-based billing (UBB) and consume Copilot Credits. We are also introducing general availability of Copilot in OneDrive, which follows the same licensing structure as SharePoint. Read more about Copilot in SharePoint and OneDrive in the blog.
  • General availability begins rolling out later this month. Tenant availability may follow as rollout progresses.
  • To prepare: No action is required to continue using capabilities included with the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Admins can control who can access advanced SharePoint capabilities through UBB by going to Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management. Existing cost management policies may automatically include newly available services. Existing PowerShell opt-out settings for the Public Preview of Copilot in SharePoint will continue to be honored until November 1st; after that, manage availability through SharePoint site AI settings.

Business Applications in Work IQ:

  • Work IQ now includes Dynamics 365 Sales, Dynamics 365 Customer Service, and Power Platform data, enabling Copilot to ground responses and tasks on business and productivity data. Read more in the blog.
  • These updates will start rolling out in public preview later this month.
  • To prepare: Admins can configure Dynamics 365 and Power Platform data sources for Copilot in the Power Platform admin center. Admins can also manage the availability of business applications in Copilot in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Settings, and access through the Work IQ Model Context Protocol (MCP) under Agents > Tools.

[Action required / Recommendations:]

In addition to the guidance listed in the individual updates above:

  • A spending policy is required for users to access capabilities available through Usage-based billing. Enable Copilot Credit consumption and configure spending policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center under Copilot > Cost management. Educate users about usage-based billing scenarios and how to request access through IT. Learn more about spending policy and usage-based billing in the blog and message center post titled: Evolving Copilot pricing and new FinOps capabilities for AI.
  • Monitor this post for updated availability and deployment details.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft 365 Backup: Full workload backup for SharePoint, OneDrive, and Exchange
item.description:
[What and Why:]

We are introducing Full Workload Backup for Microsoft 365 Backup, a new capability that allows admins to quickly protect an entire workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, or Exchange) with a single policy. This feature automatically includes all existing and newly created artifacts that are not already covered by custom policies, helping organizations improve data protection coverage, reduce administrative overhead, and ensure continuous backup for critical business data at scale.

This enhancement supports enterprise-ready data protection and automation, enabling organizations to safeguard content more efficiently while maintaining control through existing policy configurations.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 464990.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Public Preview (Worldwide): We will begin rolling out in early July 2026 and expect to complete by mid-July 2026.
  • General Availability: We will begin rolling out in mid-September 2026 and expect to complete by mid-October 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Admins managing Microsoft 365 Backup policies
  • Organizations currently using or planning to use Microsoft 365 Backup

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Backup
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Exchange Online

What will happen:

  • A new option to back up all artifacts within a selected workload will be available.
  • Admins can enable Full Workload Backup per workload (SharePoint, OneDrive, Exchange).
  • All eligible artifacts not covered by existing custom backup policies will be automatically protected.
  • Newly created artifacts will be included in backup coverage automatically on subsequent runs.
  • Existing custom backup policies will continue to take precedence and remain unchanged.

  • Evaluate whether Full Workload Backup aligns with your data protection strategy.

  • Update internal documentation if you manage backup procedures.

  1. Go to the Microsoft 365 Backup dashboard in the Microsoft 365 admin center. 
  2. Select the workload you want to protect and choose the option to back up all artifacts. 
  3. (Optional) Upload a CSV file on the Exclude sites step to exclude specific sites from the scope of the policy.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Unified management of app and agent availability and installation in Teams, Outlook, and the Microsoft 365 app
item.description:
Updated October 1, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

What it is

Microsoft is rolling out a new feature to streamline how app and agent availability and installation is managed across Teams, Outlook, and Microsoft 365 Copilot. Until now, IT admins configured availability and installation settings separately in both the Microsoft 365 Admin Center (MAC) and the Teams Admin Center (TAC), which led to mismatches. With this update, you’ll be able to unify availability and installation policies for apps and agents across both portals, making app management more consistent and efficient.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931, 485712 and 503105.

When this will happen: 

  • App and agent AVAILABILITY unification (section A): Rollout began in late September 2025. The Phase 3 timeline will be announced separately, at least 60 days before that phase begins.
  • App and agent INSTALLATION unification (section B): Rollout begins at the end of September 2026. 

A: Unify app availability across admin centers

1. Phase 1 – Default Tenant Unification of App/Agent Availability

We will begin rolling out this feature at the end of September 2025. This initial phase targets tenants that have never modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock in either the Microsoft 365 admin center or the Teams admin center. At the end of this phase, agent and app manageability will be unified across both Microsoft 365 admin center and Teams admin center ensuring agent and Microsoft 365 apps availability policies are in alignment for all future administrative changes. This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 393931.

2.Phase 2 – Modified Tenants Unification of App/Agent Availability

This phase targets tenants that have previously modified their organization-wide defaults, app availability, or block/unblock settings in either admin center. These tenants will be transitioned to a unified management experience across both Microsoft 365 and Teams admin centers.

  • For tenants with no agent or app availability differences across both admin centers, guidance will be provided to help maintain unified availability policy for all future changes.

  • As part of this phase we will also enable administrators to manage Microsoft 365 certified SaaS applications within their tenant through org-wide settings for third-party apps. This has been rolled out completely for all tenants.
  • This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 485712 & 503105.

This phase has been fully rolled out to all tenants. Tenants can choose to align through the wizard experience available in Teams admin center.

Note: In this phase, no changes will be applied to org-wide settings or app-level settings without administrator action.

3. Phase 3 – Automatic Unification (Future)

Tenants that have not taken action to unify availability through the wizard experience released in Phase 1 and Phase 2 will have their availability automatically unified across MAC and TAC as part of this phase. We will inform customers of the timeline and additional details at least 60 days in advance before this phase begins.

B: Unified app and agent installation management 

This capability unifies installation management across the Teams admin center and Microsoft 365 admin center. Administrators can manage supported app and agent installations from either portal, with changes synchronized across both admin centers. 

Who receives this capability? 

Tenants whose app and agent availability has been unified through any of the phases described in section A are eligible. Once rollout begins, this capability will be automatically enabled for tenants whose availability is already unified as part of Section A. Tenants that unify their availability later will receive this capability automatically once unified. 

Note: This capability is separate from availability unification described in section A . It does not automatically unify app or agent availability. 

When will it roll out? 

Rollout will begin at the end of September 2026 for eligible tenants. This date applies only to installation management (section B). 

Is administrator action required? 

No additional action is required to enable installation unification for eligible tenants. Existing installation assignments for supported apps and agents will be synchronized across both admin centers.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Skills in Copilot Chat
item.description:

Here is a summary of the features in this release:

  • Skills for end users: Users can create and edit skills, upload existing skills, and share skills with others. They can use skills deployed by their admin or public skills published by Independent Software Vendors. Users can choose whether Copilot can automatically invoke skills or explicitly select one from the new “Agents and Skills” section in Context IQ. For more information about the Context IQ experience, see the related Message Center post MC1479519.
  • Skill deployment by admins: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, admins can deploy, install, or block skills and plugins that contain skills and connectors. With this release, these plugins will be available in both Copilot Chat and Copilot Cowork. For more information about centralized plugin controls, see our recent announcement on plugins. Admins can also use the Tools view to review all skills created by users in Copilot Chat.
  • Agent Store to include plugins: The “Agent store” in Copilot Chat is evolving to include plugins; see our recent announcement on plugins for context. With this release, users can discover agents, skills, and plugins containing skills in the Store. Discoverability of connector-only plugins in Store is not part of this release and will be added as a follow up, making all plugins available there. Until then, connectors will remain available through the Data Sources menu in Chat.
  • Use across Cowork and Chat: Skills created in Copilot Chat can also be used in Cowork. Plugins deployed from the Microsoft 365 admin center will be available in both Copilot Chat and Copilot Cowork. However, skills created in Copilot Cowork are available in Copilot Chat only if they are shared.
  • Developer tools: User-built skills and plugins created with WIQ Dev Tools or Agents Toolkit will also be available in Copilot Chat.

Skills in Copilot Chat will roll out to Information Barriers tenants in November. In tenants where Information Barriers are enabled, users can create skills for personal use and use skills deployed by their admin or use public skills published by Independent Software Vendors. Sharing user-created skills is not currently supported but will be enabled in the future in accordance with Information Barriers policies.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Graph: New tenant controls for retirement of non-standard file API tokens
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is retiring pre-authenticated URLs, also known as tempauth URLs, from SharePoint Online and OneDrive. Beginning April 1, 2027, selected Microsoft Graph file APIs will no longer return URLs that contain embedded authentication information and will no longer issue HTTP 302 redirects to those URLs.

To help organizations prepare, new SharePoint Online tenant controls are coming soon in a future release of Microsoft SharePoint Online PowerShell. These controls will allow administrators to enable updated Microsoft Graph URL behavior for specific applications before the retirement date. This gives organizations time to validate application compatibility, improve security posture, and transition to standard Microsoft Entra ID authentication before the change takes effect.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Service change (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in early April 2027 and expected to complete in late April 2027

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Administrators responsible for Microsoft Graph, SharePoint Online, OneDrive, application integrations, and tenant security
  • Owners of third-party applications, line-of-business applications, custom applications, and automation solutions that use affected Microsoft Graph file APIs
  • Organizations using applications that follow redirects or rely on URLs containing embedded authentication information

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Graph
  • SharePoint Online
  • OneDrive
  • Microsoft Entra ID
  • Third-party and custom applications that consume Microsoft Graph file APIs

What will happen

Applications using affected Microsoft Graph APIs may currently receive:

  • SharePoint Online download, upload, monitor, preview, version, or similar URLs that contain temporary authentication information.
  • Media service URLs that contain temporary authentication information.
  • HTTP 302 redirects to URLs containing embedded authentication information.

After the change:

  • Applications configured to use supported Microsoft Graph URL alternatives will receive Microsoft Graph URLs and continue authenticating with Microsoft Graph access tokens.
  • APIs that currently return HTTP 302 redirects to temporary authentication URLs will instead return content directly.
  • SharePoint Online URLs returned by affected APIs will no longer contain embedded temporary authentication information.
  • Applications accessing SharePoint Online URLs directly will need a valid Microsoft Entra ID access token for the SharePoint Online resource.
  • Requests made directly to SharePoint APIs rather than through Microsoft Graph are not affected by the tenant control setting.
  • Applications that store, inspect, or redeem URLs containing embedded authentication tokens may stop functioning if not updated before April 1, 2027.
  • The change is not enabled by default through tenant controls. Administrators must choose which application IDs participate in testing and validation.

Affected API families include:

  • File download and content APIs
  • createUploadSession APIs
  • Copy APIs and long-running action monitors
  • Preview APIs
  • Thumbnail APIs
  • Version APIs
  • Format conversion APIs

[Action required and recommendations]

Administrators should begin validation before April 1, 2027.

Recommended actions:

  • Identify applications that obtain file, version, thumbnail, preview, upload-session, or copy-operation URLs through Microsoft Graph.
  • Review whether applications inspect, store, or redeem URLs containing embedded authentication information.
  • Verify that applications can process direct content responses instead of relying on HTTP 302 redirects.
  • Confirm applications can obtain and send the appropriate Microsoft Entra ID access token when calling Microsoft Graph or SharePoint Online endpoints.
  • Enable the new tenant setting for a limited set of application IDs and validate application behavior.
  • Monitor application errors, authentication failures, and sign-in activity during testing.
  • Expand the configuration to additional applications after successful validation.
  • Contact application vendors and internal application owners to confirm support plans and timelines for affected applications.
  • Communicate this upcoming change to development and application support teams.

No action is required if:

  • Your organization does not use the affected APIs.
  • Applications already use direct Microsoft Graph content endpoints and standard Microsoft Entra ID authentication.

Learn more

  • Clear-SPOTenantPreAuthSettings (Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell) | Microsoft Learn
  • Get-SPOTenantPreAuthSettings (Microsoft.Online.SharePoint.PowerShell) | Microsoft Learn
  • Get started with the SharePoint Online Management Shell | Microsoft Learn
  • OAuth 2.0 and OpenID Connect protocols - Microsoft identity platform | Microsoft Learn
  • Pre-authenticated (tempauth) URLs are retiring: move to Microsoft Entra ID tokens before April 1, 2027 - Microsoft 365 Developer Blog

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. New SharePoint Online tenant controls are being introduced to allow administrators to opt specific application IDs into the updated authentication behavior before the retirement date. Customers should review documentation to determine available scoping and configuration options. Regarding controlled by EntraID Group membership, I do not think that applies. These are SharePoint Online PowerShell cmdlets.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Planner: Introducing Local Custom Fields
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing Custom Fields in Microsoft Planner, enabling users to tailor plans to match the way their teams work. Users can add Text, Number, Date, Yes/No, and Choice fields to capture information that matters to their workflows and manage that information across Board, Grid, and Task details.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by early November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with a Planner Premium P1, P3, or P5 license
  • Users with a Microsoft 365 license

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Planner

What will happen

  • Users with a Planner Premium P1, P3, or P5 license will be able to create, edit, and manage Custom Fields and their values.
  • Users with a Microsoft 365 license can view Custom Fields and values as read-only and export them but cannot create or edit them.
  • Users can add up to 10 custom fields with 255 characters each to tasks in a plan for information beyond Planner's built-in fields. Available types are Text, Number, Date, Yes/No, and Choice, and field names can be up to 255 characters.
  • Choice fields are single-select and can contain 2 to 25 colored options.
  • Field values can be viewed and updated across Board, Grid, and Task details and used for sorting, filtering, grouping, and bulk editing.
  • This feature is optional. Existing plans are not affected unless users add Custom Fields.
  • Existing compliance capabilities cover custom field data, including Unified Audit Log, eDiscovery, Microsoft Information Protection through inherited plan-level labels, and Data Lifecycle Management.

[Action required and recommendations]

No tenant-level configuration or admin setup is required to enable Custom Fields. We recommend that you:

  • Ensure users who need to create or edit Custom Fields have a Planner Premium P1, P3, or P5 license. Microsoft 365 users will have read-only access.
  • Inform users about the supported field types, the limit of 10 fields per plan, and that Choice fields are single-select with 2 to 25 options.
  • Advise users that deleting a custom field or choice option is permanent and cannot be undone, and that deleting a choice option clears affected values.
  • Remind users to follow your organization's data-handling policies. Custom field data is included in audit, eDiscovery, Microsoft Information Protection, and data lifecycle processes.

[Learn more]

We will update this post with new documentation.

[Compliance considerations]

Does the change store new customer data?

  • Yes. Custom field names and values that users create on tasks (up to 10 fields per plan) are stored as part of plan/task data.

Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed (e.g., documents, emails, chats, etc.)? 

  • No. Existing task and plan data is unchanged. Custom fields are additive metadata on tasks.

Does the change modify, interrupt, or disable any of the following Microsoft Purview capabilities?

  • Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies or enforcement
    • No.
  • Information Protection labels or sensitive information types
    • No.
  • Conditional Access policies
    • No.
  • Audit logging capabilities
    • No. Custom field edits are logged in Task History and flow to the Unified Audit Log.
  • eDiscovery or Content Search
    • No.
  • Encryption methods or key management
    • No. Data uses existing service encryption.
  • Retention policies, holds, or deletion workflows
    • No. Custom field data follows the existing task/plan lifecycle (deleted when the task/plan is deleted).

Does the change alter how admins can monitor, report on, or demonstrate compliance activities (e.g., Purview or admin reporting)?

  • No. Existing Purview and admin reporting continue to work; custom field activity appears in audit logs like other task edits.

Does the change modify how users can access, export, delete, or correct their personal data within Microsoft 365 services (GDPR Data Subject Rights)?

  • No. Users can view, edit, and export custom field values (Export to Excel), and the data is deleted along with the task or plan it belongs to.

[What and Why:]

Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint is introducing the built-in Clarify my thinking skill for PowerPoint on web. This skill was previously referred to as “GrillMe” and has been renamed to use more customer-friendly wording.

With this skill, users can ask Copilot to answer questions that help sharpen their ideas and improve their presentation before sharing or presenting. This can help users refine messaging, clarify points, and strengthen the overall quality of a presentation.

[Rollout Schedule:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins on October 8, 2026.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users with access to Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint on web.
  • Organizations that use Copilot in PowerPoint to draft, refine, or review presentation content.

Platforms/Services:

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft PowerPoint on web

What will happen:

  • Users will see the built-in Clarify my thinking skill in Copilot for PowerPoint.
  • The skill helps users answer questions designed to sharpen ideas and improve presentation clarity.
  • The feature is enabled as part of the existing Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint experience.
  • Existing Microsoft 365 Copilot admin controls and licensing requirements continue to apply.

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

No admin action is required before rollout.

You may want to inform users that the Clarify my thinking skill is becoming available in Copilot for PowerPoint and update any internal Copilot guidance or training materials as appropriate.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? Yes. The Clarify my thinking skill uses Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint to analyze presentation content and generate feedback.
  • Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Yes. The skill gives users a new prompt-based way to request presentation feedback from Copilot in PowerPoint.
